statements.status_notes: GHSA-gq4g-fpc9-vjfq affects Webauthn\SimpleFakeCredentialGenerator when it is constructed without a secret: the decoy credential list for an unknown username becomes predictable, weakening username enumeration protection. The upstream fix in web-auth/webauthn-lib 5.3.5 changes only that class (https://github.com/web-auth/webauthn-framework/security/advisories/GHSA-gq4g-fpc9-vjfq). Nextcloud does not use this class. In the Nextcloud 34.0.3 release tree the only references to FakeCredentialGenerator or SimpleFakeCredentialGenerator are the two class files themselves and the Composer autoload map; nothing in webauthn-lib 4.9.1, in Nextcloud core (lib/private/Authentication/WebAuthn) or in any shipped app instantiates or injects it. Nextcloud builds PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions directly in its WebAuthn Manager, so the vulnerable code path is never executed.
